decision: Treat Grok reliability as a protocol and runner migration, not a one-method patch
why: Plan approval, questions, cancellation reasons, account rotation, fallbacks, and reconnects share the same ACP boundary

decision: Sequence grounding, design arena, failing protocol tests, implementation units, blast-radius checks, checkout gate, deploy, and live verification
why: Each unit must end with executable evidence before the next starts

decision: Reuse the actor-backed Ask lifecycle and add acknowledged host answer delivery
why: The UI answer is durable, but the current server-to-host delivery can be lost after commit and before socket write

decision: Use a server-owned logical coordinator and one disposable host per model/account attempt
why: A long-lived credential-lease host has cumulative exposure to every rotated account; per-attempt hosts preserve the existing one-account blast radius

decision: Auto-approve exit_plan_mode only for explicitly unattended runs; cancel ordinary Grok questions without a human route
why: Plan continuation does not grant tools, while fabricating questionnaire answers would; existing tool and MCP policy remains fail-closed

decision: Support Grok as an explicit fallback destination without adding it to the implicit global fallback order
why: Protocol parity and operator spend policy are separate decisions

decision: Negotiate Grok 1.0.13 grok.com auth while retaining cached_token rolling compatibility
why: The installed client no longer offers the old hard-coded method

decision: Require a real installed-client plan-mode turn before the repository gate
why: The deterministic peer proves our side of the wire but cannot prove Grok accepts the response

decision: Persist logical fallback policy on every physical host and fence pool mutation by provider/model/account identity
why: A gateway restart must not turn the current account's usage receipt into the final logical result

decision: Isolate unit-test fixture Git repos from machine-wide hooks and raise the isolated test timeout to 30s
why: The required repository gate must not depend on Jack's global author/pre-commit policy, and ACP/restart fixtures legitimately exceed Bun's 5s default under one-file process isolation

decision: Run focused Grok/recovery regression suites before the full gate
why: The change crosses ACP wire handling, host coordination, durable ask replay, and runner protocol
evidence: bun test acp-runner.test.ts asks-restart.test.ts grok-acp-extension.test.ts host-coordinator.test.ts protocol/runner.test.ts --timeout 30000: 63 pass

decision: Run the required repository gate after fixing the runner boundary
why: Commit is only allowed after the full project check passes
evidence: bun run check: format:check, typecheck, lint, 700 isolated unit files, strict transcript snapshots

decision: Close restart, account-identity, direct-route, and documentation gaps found by independent reviewers
why: A physical terminal cannot erase logical recovery state, a mutable spec cannot poison another account, and direct ACP routes cannot silently lose their MCP tools
evidence: host-client.ts; host-coordinator.test.ts; goal-runner.ts; Slack model fence; docs/security-model.md

decision: Require Grok CLI 1.0.16 for MCP form elicitation
why: Stable 1.0.13 rejects form elicitation before calling the ACP client; the 1.0.16 bridge reaches x.ai/mcp/elicit and publishes its exact outcome-tagged response schema
evidence: installed 1.0.13 and isolated 1.0.16 probes; xai-org/grok-build bb7f39d5858cbf5e00de639367f59debbdcb0138

decision: Return outcome accept|decline|cancel for xAI private MCP elicitation while retaining action accept|decline|cancel for standard ACP
why: xAI's private McpElicitExtResponse is an outcome-tagged enum even though the downstream MCP ElicitResult is action-tagged

decision: Make the installed-client elicitation probe inspect the actual MCP result
why: A model can print the requested terminal marker after a failed tool, so terminal text alone was a false-positive oracle
evidence: scripts/verify-acp-provider.ts; 1.0.13 exits 1 with unsupported form; isolated 1.0.16 exits 0 with action accept and label stable

decision: Re-run focused compatibility and route regressions after blast-radius fixes
why: The post-review changes touch Grok wire conversion, host recovery, Slack routing, and goal MCP ownership
evidence: bun test focused 8 files: 104 pass; bun run typecheck; check-module-side-effects: 495 modules clean

decision: Run the complete repository gate after every compatibility and blast-radius correction
why: The build contract requires the exact final checkout state to pass formatting, types, lint, isolated unit tests, and strict transcript snapshots before commit
evidence: bun run check: format:check, typecheck, lint, 703 isolated unit files, strict transcript snapshots

decision: Treat the production host's Grok 1.0.13 binary as a ship blocker even though the source and image pin are correct
why: The adapter cannot provide MCP form parity until the live host runs the 1.0.16 private elicitation bridge; changing the default before that would recreate a known route failure

decision: Activate Grok Build 1.0.16 on the host and rebuild the runner image from the exact deployed release
why: The source pin alone does not update a running host or previously built sandbox image
evidence: production host grok --version; opensession-runner:be6f77a86 image probe; direct normal and elicitation probes

decision: Do not change the default after the first public-route probe
why: Grok discovered the correct Open Session tool through search_tool but ended the prompt before invoking it; a terminal marker alone would hide this false success

decision: Treat a successful search_tool followed by end_turn and no non-search tool call as an ACP compatibility terminal
why: Official prompt_complete is a true prompt terminal, and the behavior reproduced across accounts and host/sandbox routes; the adapter must continue the same provider session rather than waiting for a user retry
evidence: xAI Grok Build source; production ACP transcripts and client logs

decision: Continue the same Grok ACP session at most twice, then emit one exact transient error eligible for the existing model fallback
why: A bounded structural predicate avoids parsing model prose, prevents infinite loops, preserves account health, and makes repeated false success recoverable by the provider-neutral fallback walk

decision: Continue only when typed Grok SearchTool raw output reports a positive integer result_count
why: A completed zero-result search is a valid terminal answer and must not trigger retries or fallback; pinned Grok 1.0.16 serializes SearchToolOutput with this authoritative count
evidence: xAI acp_conversion.rs and search_tool/mod.rs; zero-match regression; one-session setup assertion

decision: Run the complete repository gate after the final search-result refinement
why: The final checkout state must pass the build contract, not only the earlier broader predicate
evidence: bun run check: format, typecheck, lint, 703 isolated unit files, strict transcript snapshots

decision: Close the final false-positive and same-session proof gaps before shipping
why: The adapter should intervene only for actionable discovery and the test must independently prove one provider session across the internal continuation
evidence: gpt-5.5 final review; follow-up review after corrections
